verdicts.explanation: The paper states the highest ionic conductivity, 2.3×10-5 S cm-1, is for the Er2O3 nanofiller sample (PPLE, 10 wt.%), measured by EIS at room temperature. Origin is experimental and the solution-cast method matches the paper.

The paper states 'The ionic conductivity of pure polymer blend was 6.4×10-10 S cm-1' from its own EIS measurements at room temperature, so the material, value, unit, temperature and origin all check out.

The sentence pairs 6.40×10-10 and 7.10×10-7 S cm-1 'respectively' with the pure blend and the polymer salt system, and both are bulk-resistance values from the impedance plot at room temperature. The 'bulk' kind is supported, and the JPL value of 4.66×10-7 is correctly left unrecorded.
